paper_type_evidence.quote: We report continuum and C$^{18}$O (2–1) observations of the VLA 1623-2417 protostellar system at 50 au angular resolution as part of the ALMA Large Program FAUST.

The VLA 1623 protostellar system was observed between October 2018 and March 2020 as part of the ALMA Large Program, FAUST (Fifty AU STudy of the chemistry in the disk/envelope system of Solar-like protostars; 2018.1.01205.L, PI: S. Yamamoto, (cite: Codella2022)).

evidence.quote: VLA1623 is located in Ophiuchus A at a distance, $d$, of 131 pc (cite: Gagne2018), and consists of four protostellar sources: VLA 1623A, a close Class 0 binary, with separation between the components (A1 and A2) of $\sim 30$ au, surrounded by a circumbinary disk; VLA 1623B, a Class 0 protostar located $\sim130$ au West of VLA 1623A and associated with an edge-on disk; and VLA 1623W, classified as a Class I protostar and located $\sim1300$ au West of the A binary, also associated with an edge-on disk (cite: Bontemps1997; Murillo2013SED; Harris2018; Kawabe2018).
The observations were centered at $\alpha_{\rm 2000}$ = 16${^h}$26${^m}$26${^s}$.392, $\delta_{\rm 2000}$ = –24$^\circ$24$'$30$''$.69.

question.value: Investigate the gas in the disk of VLA 1623W and its dynamical interaction with the other protostellar sources in the VLA 1623 multiple protostellar system using ALMA 1.3 mm continuum and C18O (2-1) observations.

evidence.quote: In this paper, we report ALMA observations of C$^{18}$O (2–1) and continuum emission at 1.3 mm used to investigate the gas in the disk of VLA 1623W, and the source dynamical interaction with the other protostellar sources in the VLA 1623 multiple protostellar system.

The VLA 1623 protostellar system was observed between October 2018 and March 2020 as part of the ALMA Large Program, FAUST (Fifty AU STudy of the chemistry in the disk/envelope system of Solar-like protostars; 2018.1.01205.L, PI: S. Yamamoto, (cite: Codella2022)).
The raw data will be available on the ALMA archive at the end of the proprietary period (ADS/JAO.ALMA#2018.1.01205.L).
The 1.3 mm continuum probes the disks of VLA 1623A, B, and W, and the circumbinary disk of the A1+A2 binary.
We observed in the Band 6 frequency range 216–234 GHz, using the 12-m array (C43-4 and C43-1) and 7-m array of the Atacama Compact Array (ACA).

analysis_steps.goal: Estimate dynamical mass of VLA 1623W from high-velocity C18O disk kinematics

method.value: Measure radial peak distances of symmetric high-velocity C18O channels and apply Keplerian rotation formula M_dyn = r * V^2 / G

evidence.loc: The gas towards the disk of VLA 1623W
evidence.quote: We therefore use the emission in the channels at radial velocities of $\pm$ 2.8 and $\pm$ 3.0 km s$^{-1}$ to derive an estimate of the VLA 1623W dynamical mass, $M_{\rm dyn}$. The emission in these channels peak at a radial distance of 0.37$''$ and 0.33$''$. By assuming Keplerian motion we estimate a dynamical mass, $$\begin{equation} M_{dyn} = r \frac{V^{2}}{G} \end{equation}$$ where $r$ and $V$ are the distance and velocity of the blue- and red-shifted peaks, deprojected for the disk inclination of 80$\ensuremath{^\circ}$.

findings_qualitative.value: Three C18O streamers (N, S1, S2) extending over >1000 au spatially and kinematically connect the VLA 1623A+B envelope and outflow cavities with the disk of VLA 1623W.

findings_qualitative.value: The formation of VLA 1623W in an adjacent Ophiuchus A ridge is unlikely because its systemic velocity (+1.6 km/s) differs from that of the ridges (+3 to +4 km/s) and VLA 1623AB (+3.8 km/s).

claims.hypothesis: Compact high-velocity C18O (2-1) emission towards VLA 1623W traces a Keplerian rotating disk around the protostar.
claims.experiment: Image high-velocity C18O (2-1) emission (-2.6 to +5.8 km/s) using the 12-m array at ~50 au resolution and measure peak radial offsets in symmetric velocity channels (+/- 2.8 and +/- 3.0 km/s).
claims.result: Compact blue- and red-shifted emission is detected along the disk major axis (PA ~ 10 deg) centered on V_sys = +1.6 km/s, peaking at smaller radii for higher velocities, yielding a dynamical mass M_dyn = 0.45 +/- 0.08 M_odot.
claims.finding: C18O (2-1) reveals for the first time Keplerian rotating molecular gas in the disk of VLA 1623W, constraining its central protostellar mass to 0.45 +/- 0.08 M_odot.

evidence.loc: The gas towards the disk of VLA 1623W
evidence.quote: In the channel maps at high velocities, instead, the peaks of the blue- and red-shifted emission are located along the disk major axis, and the emission is more compact and peaks at smaller distances for increasing velocities with respect to V$_{\rm sys}$(W) as expected in a Keplerian rotating disk.

evidence.loc: The gas towards the disk of VLA 1623W
evidence.quote: By assuming Keplerian motion we estimate a dynamical mass, $$\begin{equation} M_{dyn} = r \frac{V^{2}}{G} \end{equation}$$ where $r$ and $V$ are the distance and velocity of the blue- and red-shifted peaks, deprojected for the disk inclination of 80$\ensuremath{^\circ}$. The estimated dynamical mass is $0.45 \pm 0.08$ M$_{\odot}$.

claims.hypothesis: VLA 1623W is physically and kinematically connected to the VLA 1623A+B system rather than being an unrelated foreground or background object.
claims.experiment: Map large-scale low-velocity C18O (2-1) emission (+0.2 to +3.0 km/s) using combined 12-m and 7-m ACA data.
claims.result: Three arc-like streamers (N, S1, S2) extending >1000 au connect the northern blueshifted and southern redshifted outflow cavities/envelope of VLA 1623A+B to the corresponding blueshifted and redshifted sides of the VLA 1623W disk.
claims.finding: VLA 1623W is spatially and kinematically linked to the VLA 1623A+B system via large-scale molecular streamers.

evidence.loc: The streamers connecting VLA 1623W with the A+B system
evidence.quote: the blueshifted outflow cavity/streamer north of VLA1623A connects with the northern blueshifted side of the VLA 1623W edge-on disk, while the redshifted outflow cavity/streamer south of VLA 1623A connects with the southern redshifted side of the VLA 1623W disk. This indicates that the protostellar sources A and W are kinematically linked.

evidence.loc: Discussion: On the origin of VLA 1623W
evidence.quote: On the other hand, the molecular streamers connecting the disk of VLA 1623W with the envelope/cavities of VLA 1623A and VLA1623B suggest that VLA 1623W is not a background or foreground object.

claims.hypothesis: VLA 1623W was ejected from the VLA 1623A+B multiple system, which can be tested via plane-of-sky proper motion measurements.
claims.experiment: Measure relative astrometric separations between VLA 1623W and sources A and B across a 27.7-year baseline using 1991.8 VLA X-band (3.6 cm) and 2019.5 ALMA Band 6 (1.3 mm) continuum images.
claims.result: Relative plane-of-sky velocities are -4.4 +/- 1.47 km/s (A with respect to W) and -3.5 +/- 1.26 km/s (B with respect to W), showing no significant difference at the 3-sigma level, while the required ejection velocity (~0.65 km/s) is below the measurement uncertainty (~1.3-1.5 km/s).
claims.finding: Available proper motion measurements can neither confirm nor rule out the ejection scenario.

evidence.quote: Based on the above estimates, there is no significant difference in tangential velocity between VLA 1623W and A (or B) at the three sigma level. However, in the ejection scenario the velocity needed for VLA 1623W to move away from A+B up to a distance of $\sim10\ensuremath{''}$ in 10$^4$ years (i.e., the typical Class 0 age) is only 0.65 km s$^{-1}$, i.e. below the uncertainty associated with our proper motion measurements ($\sim 1.3-1.5$ km s$^{-1}$).
Thus, the ejection scenario can be neither ruled out nor confirmed by the available proper motion.

why_this_data.value: ALMA Band 6 continuum and C18O (2-1) observations combining 12-m (C43-4, C43-1) and 7-m ACA arrays simultaneously resolve the ~50 au disk kinematics and recover extended streamer emission up to ~3000 au.

evidence.quote: (2) combining the data taken with the 12-m and the 7-m arrays to recover emission extending up to $\sim 3000$ au

why_this_method.value: Uniform weighting (robust = -2.0) was chosen for continuum to achieve highest angular resolution, whereas robust = 0.5 was chosen for C18O to optimize signal-to-noise; high-velocity channels (>= 2.8 km/s) on the 12-m-only cube were used for dynamical mass estimation to avoid contamination from large-scale streamers.

evidence.quote: We adopted Briggs weighting with a robustness parameter of $-2.0$ (uniform weighting) for the continuum to obtain the highest angular resolution (beam: 0.42$''$ $\times$ 0.32$''$, PA=$-65^\circ$). On the other hand, a robustness parameter of $0.5$ was employed for the molecular emission to optimize the signal-to-noise, consistently with the previous FAUST paper on VLA 1623 (cite: Ohashi2022).

evidence.loc: The gas towards the disk of VLA 1623W
evidence.quote: In this case, only the combined 12-m array is used to minimise contamination from the large scale emission.

evidence.loc: The gas towards the disk of VLA 1623W
evidence.quote: Indeed, we find that the blue-shifted disk side is brighter than the red-shifted one up to velocities of $\pm 2.6$ km s$^{-1}$ with respect to systemic, likely due to contamination from the extended streamers observed at larger scales (see Sect. 0.0.1). At higher velocities the emission from each disk side is symmetric. We therefore use the emission in the channels at radial velocities of $\pm$ 2.8 and $\pm$ 3.0 km s$^{-1}$ to derive an estimate of the VLA 1623W dynamical mass, $M_{\rm dyn}$.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Rejected that elongated C18O emission North and South of VLA 1623W is a jet or outflow, because it is aligned along the disk PA rather than perpendicular to it.

evidence.quote: Moreover, C$^{18}$O shows emission towards the VLA 1623W disk continuum, as well as an elongated structure to the North and to the South of W, roughly along the disk position angle. This elongated emission cannot be due to a jet or an outflow as it is not perpendicular to the disk PA.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Considered and deemed unlikely that VLA 1623W formed in a separate adjacent Ophiuchus A ridge interacting gravitationally with VLA 1623AB, because the systemic velocity of W (+1.6 km/s) differs from that of both adjacent ridges (+3 to +4 km/s) and VLA 1623AB (+3.8 km/s).

evidence.loc: Hypothesis 1: formation in a separate core
evidence.quote: However, the maps by (cite: Chen2018) indicate that the systemic velocity of the two adjacent ridges is similar (both being between +3 and +4 km s$^{-1}$), while our observations indicate that VLA 1623W has a systemic velocity of $+1.6$ km s$^{-1}$, which differs from the systemic velocity of VLA 1623AB ($+3.8$ km s$^{-1}$) and the two ridges. Thus, this first scenario is unlikely.

limitations_admitted.value: Angular resolution of the 1.3 mm continuum (~0.42'' x 0.32'') is too low to resolve the close binary components VLA 1623A1 and A2 (~30 au separation).

evidence.quote: The protostellar sources A, B, and W are detected, as well as the circumbinary disk, but the angular resolution is too low to disentangle the close binary components, A1 and A2, resolved by (cite: Harris2018) at 0.9 mm (separation $\sim 30$ au).

limitations_admitted.value: Derived disk mass is subject to large uncertainties from assuming a gas-to-dust ratio of 100 (upper limit if lower) and optically thin dust emission (lower limit if optically thick), plus 10% flux calibration uncertainty and temperature range (20-50 K).

evidence.quote: Moreover, the derived disk mass is affected by large uncertainty due to: (i) the assumption on the gas-to-dust ratio. If this is lower than 100 (cite: Ansdell2016), the estimated disk mass should be regarded as an upper limit; (ii) the assumption that the dust continuum emission is optically thin. If the emission is optically thick, the estimated disk mass is a lower limit.

limitations_admitted.value: Low-velocity C18O emission towards the disk of VLA 1623W (up to +/- 2.6 km/s from systemic) is contaminated by extended emission from the streamers and/or residual envelope.

evidence.loc: The gas towards the disk of VLA 1623W
evidence.quote: Indeed, we find that the blue-shifted disk side is brighter than the red-shifted one up to velocities of $\pm 2.6$ km s$^{-1}$ with respect to systemic, likely due to contamination from the extended streamers observed at larger scales (see Sect. 0.0.1).

limitations_admitted.value: Proper motion uncertainties (~1.3-1.5 km/s) are larger than the velocity required to eject VLA 1623W over ~10'' in 10^4 yr (0.65 km/s), preventing confirmation or rejection of the ejection scenario.

evidence.quote: However, in the ejection scenario the velocity needed for VLA 1623W to move away from A+B up to a distance of $\sim10\ensuremath{''}$ in 10$^4$ years (i.e., the typical Class 0 age) is only 0.65 km s$^{-1}$, i.e. below the uncertainty associated with our proper motion measurements ($\sim 1.3-1.5$ km s$^{-1}$).

limitations_admitted.value: Line-of-sight geometry of the southern streamer with respect to VLA 1623W is unknown, leaving it ambiguous whether the 1 km/s velocity gradient traces infall onto W or outflow from W towards A+B.

evidence.quote: In the ejection scenario, the velocity gradient of 1 km s$^{-1}$ detected along the southern streamer indicates either material falling on VLA 1623W if the streamer is located in front (i.e. between W and the observer) or alternatively gas moving away from VLA 1623W towards A+B if the streamer is located on the other side of W.

referee_caveats_inferred: The dynamical mass of VLA 1623W is estimated from peak positions in just two pairs of velocity channels (+/- 2.8 and +/- 3.0 km/s) rather than full 3D forward modeling or a position-velocity diagram fit.
The edge-on disk of VLA 1623W (i ~ 80 deg) is very likely optically thick at 1.3 mm, making the optically thin dust mass formula a strong lower limit.

Comparing 3.6 cm VLA free-free/gyrosynchrotron continuum peaks with 1.3 mm ALMA thermal dust continuum peaks for proper motions assumes both wavelengths trace the exact same physical center, and that the unresolved A1+A2 binary centroid has not shifted due to orbital motion or variability.

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~50-200 GB raw visibilities for one target field across two 12-m configurations (C43-4, C43-1) and 7-m ACA in ALMA Large Program FAUST; <5 GB for final continuum image and C18O cubes
reproducibility.score_reason: The paper clearly states the ALMA project code, CASA versions, weighting schemes, beam sizes, noise levels, and exact analytical equations and parameters used to derive disk masses and dynamical masses. However, low-level imaging and self-calibration parameters (scales, thresholds, solints) are omitted.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Public ALMA Large Program data (2018.1.01205.L) with straightforward, well-specified analysis steps (2D Gaussian fitting with CASA imfit, analytical dust mass equation, and two-channel Keplerian dynamical mass calculation) yielding clear numeric benchmarks.
